programs.description:
A live retreat: four days of movement, training, breathwork, ceremony and brotherhood with Mike and his team. The in-person version of everything the programs teach.

## What it is
Two cohorts a year in Mount Shasta, California. Mornings move, afternoons go inward, and evenings are fire, food and circle.

- Daily Qi Gong and team training
- Somatic breathwork ceremony
- Sweat lodge and rite of passage
- Full-board on private land

## After you get home
You leave with a take-home practice, a private brotherhood group and an integration call one week later.

## Common questions
**Do I need to be fit?** No. Everything is scalable in the moment.

**Is it a personal-development retreat or a training camp?** Both — the training is real, and so is the inner work.

programs.description:
**Level I — Beginner.** Kettlebell Lifestyle is a 9-week personalised, multi-level kettlebell and wellness program. Level I teaches the swing variations, squats, presses, cleans and combination movements from the ground up — alongside morning routines, personalised stretching, bodyweight warm-ups and follow-along workouts.

**Level II — Intermediate.** Level II picks up where the Beginner program ends. Denser conditioning, double-bell work, snatch progressions and complexes — with the same morning routine, warm-up and stretching structure holding it all together.

Direct coaching for people who want the program adapted to their body, schedule and goals — with feedback on technique and accountability week to week.

## How it works
Book a session in the app, send your training footage ahead of time, and spend the call working on exactly what is limiting you. Every session ends with a written plan.

- Video call with Mike, 60 or 90 minutes
- Technique review on your own footage
- A written block you can follow immediately
- Session notes and history kept in the app

## Who it is for
Lifters stuck at a plateau, people coming back from injury, and coaches who want their own coaching eye sharpened.

## Common questions
**Do I have to commit to a block?** No. Single sessions are fine, though most people book a four-session block.

**What if I need to move a session?** Reschedule from your coaching page up to 24 hours before.

Mike's work on rebuilding a grounded, regulated body — breath, movement and mindset for men who want capacity that lasts beyond the gym.

## What it is
Eight weeks of daily practice built around three pillars: breath mechanics, ground-based movement, and the inner work that keeps a man steady under load.

Better sleep, a slower resting heart rate, and the ability to hold your centre in conversations and situations that used to spike you.

faq.a: Yes. The physical practices are scaled to meet you where you are. This isn't about performance. If you can walk, breathe, and move with some intention, you can do this.
faq.q: I'm not in great physical shape. Can I handle this?

faq.a: Not at all. About half the men who come are new to this. The other half are returning because they got so much from the first time. That mix is part of what makes it work.
faq.q: I've never done this kind of work before. Will I be out of place?

faq.a: You don't need to be. This work is about your relationship with yourself first. Whether you're single, partnered, a father, or not, it applies directly to where you are right now.
faq.q: What if I'm not married or don't have kids?

faq.a: You're always in charge of how far you go. Some men leave having broken something open they've been carrying for years. Some leave with a quiet shift that takes a few weeks to fully land. All of it counts. And you're guided through every step with care.
faq.q: How emotionally intense does it get?

note.title: Water retention occurs when excess fluids build up inside the body. A few of the ways this may show up:
points: Unexplained weight fluctuations in a short period of time
Your ring doesn’t fit anymore, or your stomach feels swollen
When pressed, your skin may hold an indent for a few seconds
Constipation: do I feel complete after my bowel movement? Are my stools infrequent, hard, dry, or difficult to pass?

form_questions.prompt: Did I wake up with water retention, bloating, diarrhea, or constipation?

note.body: Do you feel excited to get after it today? Are you itching to move your body and get under those bells? If not, that’s ok, we all have those days — however, consider exploring why. Explore the question: “what things are draining my zest for life and motivation to train today?”

form_questions.prompt: My willingness and motivation level for training today is?

note.body: Perform a quick body scan, examining both muscle and joint soreness/achiness. Are your muscles so sore that to the touch you could scream “ouch!”, or does it feel more mild and tolerable? If you are so sore and achy that you feel it will hamper today's training session, select “Not at all”.

form_questions.prompt: How recovered does my body feel following the prior workout?

note.body: Stress isn’t always a bad thing, however, when it occurs at a level that we cannot manage effectively, over time it can become a problem. Ask yourself honestly: “what areas of my life (both personally and professionally) are feeling most stressed right now, and to what degree are they affecting me?”

form_questions.prompt: My overall stress level today is?

options.label: Moderate — I’m experiencing some stress, but managing well

note.title: When checking in with yourself, consider:
points: How alert and ready do I feel mentally?
How good was my sleep last night?
Did I feel the need to hit the snooze button today on the alarm?
Did I need a cup of coffee to get myself going?

form_questions.prompt: Did I wake up today feeling tired, honestly?
